notes: Created run: TR-9110 (uuid 17577900, project PR-2005 / 379335744) - flag for cleanup. WHAT WORKED: path_params {project_id: 379335744}, body FLAT (not wrapped in test_run) = {run_state: 'new_run', name: '__mcp-probe-createrun-20260921', test_case_ids: [1971631, 1971632, 1975349]} - succeeded 200 on the very first attempt, no retries needed. test_case_ids takes bare NUMERIC ids (not TC-NNN strings, unlike v2's test_cases field), matching the pool's numeric ids for TC-54455/TC-54456/TC-54458 given in the task. All 3 cases attached synchronously and visible immediately in overall_progress_by_status_id (3x untested) both in the create echo and the follow-up list read. SPECIFIC-INTEREST FINDINGS (comparing create's response to the confirmed list_test_runs_by_integer_id drift, same entity, same hour, same row): project_id, is_dynamic and overall_progress are ALL typed and populated CORRECTLY in the create response (string, boolean, non-null object respectively) - this isolates all three defects cleanly to list_test_runs_by_integer_id's list serializer; the create/storage path is fine. The overall_progress null-on-list defect is proven to be a pure serializer bug rather than an eventual-consistency gap, because overall_progress_by_status_id (a sibling field) already carries the real counts on the very same freshly-created row when re-read via list_test_runs_by_integer_id seconds later - the underlying data exists, the list serializer just doesn't surface it under the 'overall_progress' key. uuid holds a plain integer on BOTH create and list, but for create this actually matches ITS OWN declared type (integer) - so 'uuid holding an integer' is a naming complaint (misleading key name), not a type-contract violation, at least for this endpoint. type and self_ui_link are declared but never emitted by either the create or the list serializer for this run - this looks like a dead/vestigial declared field shared across the whole entity's surface, not something isolated to one endpoint. observability_url is the one NEW create-specific gap this probe surfaces: declared in create_test_run_by_integer_id's own 'returns' summary, genuinely absent from the create response body, yet present and populated on the very same row when read back via list_test_runs_by_integer_id immediately after - the value is computed at creation time (it embeds the run's own build hash) but the create write-path's serializer drops it before returning, while the read-path serializer includes it. The tool's own 200-response description makes an explicit promise ('ADDS the top-level skipped_test_case_ids sibling the handlers actually render') that the live response does not keep - no skipped_test_case_ids key appeared anywhere in the body, top-level or nested, even though 0 cases were skipped (a legitimate all-succeeded case, so this isn't 'field omitted when empty' - it's just never rendered). Verdict is DRIFT: the write itself behaved exactly as declared (200, enum validated up front, all 3 cases attached, run persisted and independently verified via list_test_runs_by_integer_id), but the response body disagrees with its own declared schema in both directions (4 declared-missing fields including a top-level key the tool description explicitly promises, and 5 undeclared-returned fields: attachments, created_by, updated_by, closed_at, closed_by).
